about: Conformance vectors for the Sede view stream. A B frame payload is a 16-byte network-order header (u8 version 1, u8 flags with bit 0 the last chunk and no other bit, u16 reserved zero, u32 image sequence, u16 chunk index, u16 chunk count = ceil(image length / 65520), u32 image length 1..2097152) and a body of exactly 65520 bytes for every chunk but the last. headers: accepted headers with their fields and the body length each must carry. header_refusals: headers refused with the given body length; check is the Python diagnostic name. streams: frames read in order on a downstream view connection; announce is a view.image J document, document any other J document, chunk a B payload whose body is the image bytes from offset for length, where image byte k is k mod 251. expect lists what the reader returns in order, or refused_at names the step that refuses and closes the connection. documents: control documents each direction must accept or refuse, in their closed sets. Flag bit 1 (transfer_flag) marks a chunk of a download or upload instead of an image; its 16-byte header is u8 version 1, u8 flags (bit 0 the last chunk, bit 1 set, no other bit), u16 reserved zero, u32 transfer id from 1, u64 byte offset of the body's first byte. Every chunk but the last carries exactly 65520 body bytes and offsets are multiples of 65520; the last carries 0 to 65520 bytes, none only at offset 0. No total transfer size is bounded beyond the 64-bit offset. transfer_headers and transfer_header_refusals are the transfer analogues of headers and header_refusals, and an image header that sets flag bit 1 is refused. transfer_streams: direction names the reader, downstream for the window (which receives downloads) and upstream for the worker side (which receives uploads). setup lists the receiver calls made before any frame is read: expect a transfer with an optional exact size, grant credit in chunks, cancel locally. steps, expect and refused_at read as in streams; an expected chunk names its transfer id, offset, length, last flag and the sha256 of its body, and transfer byte k is k mod 251. A transfer chunk is refused when its transfer was not expected, arrives out of order, interleaves with another transfer or inside an image, or exceeds the credit granted; a completion is refused when it precedes the last chunk or disagrees with the bytes received in size or sha256, or with the declared size.
